questions.question: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Meissner’s plexus is present in submucosa
Myenteric plexus is present between inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle layer
Muscularis mucosa is associated with peristalsis
Villi are absent in large intestine

suspectLines.text: Layers of intestinal wall from outside to inside are:

questions.explanation:
Muscularis propria is associated with peristalsis and not muscularis mucosa. Contraction of muscularis mucosa alters absorptive and secretive surface area.

Meissner’s plexus (submucosal plexus) is present in the submucosa. The myenteric plexus (Auerbach plexus) is present between the inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle layer.

Villi are absent in the large intestine but present in the small intestine.

Layers of intestinal wall from outside to inside are:
• Serosa
• Longitudinal smooth muscle layer
• Circular smooth muscle layer
• Submucosa
• Mucosa

questions.question: Salivary amylase is inactivated by which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Salivary amylase is inactivated by the low pH of the stomach. It is rapidly denatured at pH 4 (gastric pH is 1 to 3.5). Salivary amylase is activated by chloride.

Salivary α-amylase (Ptyalin):
• Digests starch: cleaves internal α-1,4-glycosidic bonds in starch
• Optimum pH: 7
• Denatured at pH 4

Since a large portion of a meal often remains unmixed for a considerable length of time in the stomach, the salivary enzyme may account for digestion of as much as 75% of the starch present before it is denatured by gastric acid.

Note: Even in the absence of salivary amylase, there is no defect in carbohydrate digestion because pancreatic amylase is sufficient to digest all of the ingested starch.

questions.question: Rennin is present in _____

suspectLines.text: Note: Renin is produced by juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney, which hydrolyzes angiotensinogen to angiotensin I.

questions.explanation:
Rennin is present in the gastric juice. It is also called chymosin.

It is a protein-digesting enzyme (endopeptidase) found in the stomach of newborn cows. It transforms (curdles) caseinogen into insoluble casein.

In humans and in some animals that lack rennin, milk is coagulated by the action of pepsin.

Note: Renin is produced by juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney, which hydrolyzes angiotensinogen to angiotensin I.

questions.question: A patient presents with anemia and achlorhydria. After evaluation, pernicious anemia is diagnosed. Damage to which of the following cells is responsible for this condition?

suspectLines.text: Pernicious anemia occurs due to deficiency of the intrinsic factor of Castle, which is important for the absorption of vitamin B12.

questions.explanation:
Pernicious anemia develops due to autoimmune damage to the parietal cells in gastric glands.

The parietal cells secrete both HCl and intrinsic factor. Therefore, when the parietal cells are destroyed, both achlorhydria, as well as pernicious anemia, develop.

Pernicious anemia occurs due to deficiency of the intrinsic factor of Castle, which is important for the absorption of vitamin B12.

questions.question: In the stomach, H+ ions are secreted in exchange for which of the following ions?

suspectLines.text: H+ ions are secreted into the lumen of the stomach in exchange for K+ by the H+-K+ pump (H+, K+-ATPase).
• H+ and Cl- combine to form HCl.

questions.explanation:
H+ ions are secreted into the lumen of the stomach in exchange for K+ by the H+-K+ pump (H+, K+-ATPase).

Mechanism of HCl formation:
• In the parietal cells, CO2 and H2O are converted to H+ and HCO3-, catalyzed by carbonic anhydrase.
• H+ is secreted into the lumen of the stomach by the H+-K+ pump in exchange for K+.
• HCO3- moves out of the cell into the bloodstream in exchange for Cl- (Cl-/HCO3- exchange). This Cl- moves into the lumen of the stomach.
• H+ and Cl- combine to form HCl.

As HCO3- is added to the venous blood, the pH of the blood increases. This is called alkaline tide. Eventually, this HCO3- will be secreted in the pancreatic secretions to neutralize H+ in the small intestine.

Proton pump inhibitors inhibit the H+-K+ pump.

questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for increasing the HCl secretion in the gastric phase?

suspectLines.text: Gastrin stimulates H+ secretion by interaction with cholecystokinin B (CCKB) receptor on the parietal cell which secretes HCl.

questions.explanation:
HCl secretion in the gastric phase is increased by gastrin.

Gastrin stimulates H+ secretion by interaction with cholecystokinin B (CCKB) receptor on the parietal cell which secretes HCl.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the secretion from the exocrine pancreas?

suspectLines.text: It has virtually the same Na+ and K+ concentrations as in plasma. It is rich in several digestive enzymes like amylase, trypsin, chymotrypsin, lipase, elastase, etc.

questions.explanation:
Pancreatic secretion is stimulated by cholecystokinin (CCK) and Ach. It is always isotonic.

It has virtually the same Na+ and K+ concentrations as in plasma. It is rich in several digestive enzymes like amylase, trypsin, chymotrypsin, lipase, elastase, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most potent choleretic?

suspectLines.text: Note: Cholagogues cause contraction of the gallbladder. Eg. CCK.

questions.explanation:
Bile salts (chemical choleretic) are the most potent choleretics.

Any substance that increases bile secretion is called a choleretic. Bile secretion may be increased by chemical (bile salts), hormonal (Secretin), and neural (vagal stimulation) mechanisms.

Note: Cholagogues cause contraction of the gallbladder. Eg. CCK.

questions.question: Enterohepatic circulation is necessary for the secretion of _____

suspectLines.text: The enterohepatic circulation of bile salts is the recycling of bile salts between the small intestine (terminal ileum) and the liver by means of the portal vein. It occurs 6-8 times a day.

questions.explanation:
Enterohepatic circulation is necessary for the secretion of bile salts.

The enterohepatic circulation of bile salts is the recycling of bile salts between the small intestine (terminal ileum) and the liver by means of the portal vein. It occurs 6-8 times a day.

The recirculation of bile salts to the liver reduces the demand to synthesize new bile salts.

questions.question: Liver synthesizes all of the following except:

suspectLines.text: Plasma proteins synthesized by the liver are:

questions.explanation:
Immunoglobulins are not synthesized by the liver. They are produced by plasma cells.

Plasma proteins synthesized by the liver are:
• Albumin
• Coagulation/clotting factors
• Acute-phase proteins
• Steroid binding and other hormone-binding proteins

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding secretin?
questions.explanation:
Secretin increases HCO3- secretion by ductal cells of the pancreas and duodenum. It is secreted by the S cells in the upper small intestine.

Functions of secretin are:
• Primary function
• ↑ HCO3- secretion by ductal cells of pancreas and duodenum
• Other functions
• Augments the effects of CCK
• Inhibits gastrin release
• ↓ gastric acid secretion
• Contraction of pyloric sphincter
• Exerts trophic effect on the pancreas

questions.question: Which of the following is secreted by the I cells of duodenum?

suspectLines.text: I cells of the duodenum secrete CCK.

questions.explanation: I cells of the duodenum secrete CCK.

questions.question: Which of the following hormones do not act on the pancreas?

suspectLines.text: GI hormones acting on the pancreas include CCK, Secretin and GIP.

questions.explanation:
Gastrin does not act upon the pancreas. Gastrin stimulates gastric acid secretion and gastric mucosal growth.

GI hormones acting on the pancreas include CCK, Secretin and GIP.

GIP is also known as Glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide.
